outcome: Two independent teams settled the last open case of Hilbert's tenth problem for rings of integers: Koymans and Pagano (preprint, Dec 2024, using additive combinatorics and elliptic curves with full rational 2-torsion) and Alpöge, Bhargava, Ho and Shnidman (preprint, Jan 2025, using rank stability of abelian varieties in quadratic extensions) each proved that the problem has a negative (undecidable) answer for the ring of integers of every number field, closing the question the Wikipedia bullet asks.

disputes.summary: Koymans-Pagano posted first (arXiv, 2 Dec 2024) using additive combinatorics and 2-descent on elliptic curves with full rational 2-torsion. Alpöge-Bhargava-Ho-Shnidman posted a second, independent proof less than two months later (30 Jan 2025) via a rank-stability theorem for abelian varieties in quadratic extensions. Quanta Magazine reports both as independent, with Bhargava noting the two methods might be combinable for further results; no priority dispute is voiced by either team, and both are treated as full, independent resolutions of the same open case rather than a race with a single winner.

summary: The Wikipedia bullet asks for which number fields Hilbert's tenth problem (decidability of Diophantine equations over the ring of integers) holds. Before the frozen revision, this was known to be undecidable ('the problem holds' in the negative-answer sense of undecidability) for various families -- e.g. number fields with an abelian Galois group over Q, and fields with exactly one pair of complex conjugate embeddings -- but the general case for all number fields was open. Within the window, two independent groups closed it. Koymans and Pagano (arXiv:2412.01768, submitted 2 Dec 2024, revised through v3 on 24 Nov 2025 with referee feedback incorporated per the acknowledgements) proved a negative answer for Hilbert's tenth problem over every infinite ring finitely generated over Z, which includes the ring of integers of every number field. Alpöge, Bhargava, Ho and Shnidman (arXiv:2501.18774, submitted 30 Jan 2025) proved the same conclusion specifically for rings of integers of number fields via a theorem that every quadratic extension of number fields admits a rank-stable positive-rank abelian variety; that paper has since appeared in Inventiones Mathematicae (published version confirmed via Springer, 2025/2026), a journal of record, and was digested at length by Quanta Magazine (3 Feb 2025), with named experts (Barry Mazur, Andrew Granville) commenting on its significance and no expert dissent found. A further paper by Bjorn Poonen (arXiv:2510.19553, 22 Oct 2025) gives an alternative, independently derived proof of the rank-stability-implies-Diophantine theorem underlying the ABHS result, which functions as additional expert corroboration of that key lemma. Given a journal-of-record publication plus an expert-digested account (Quanta) plus an independent alternative proof of the key technical theorem, and two independent full proofs of the same negative-answer conclusion, I classify this as 'resolved' rather than merely 'claimed.' Neither paper mentions any AI, machine-learning, or automated-proof-search methods; both are entirely human-authored, traditional number-theoretic arguments (additive combinatorics/2-descent, and rank stability of abelian varieties respectively), so ai_role is 'none' with no basis_quote available. The resolution_direction is 'confirmed' because the results confirm/answer the open question (undecidability holds for all number fields), matching what most experts in the area expected/hoped would eventually be shown, rather than refuting a competing conjecture.
competing_reading: One could argue the Koymans-Pagano paper alone should be rated 'claimed' rather than folded into an overall 'resolved' verdict, since as of my research it is still formally an arXiv preprint (albeit heavily revised with referee comments incorporated) without a confirmed journal acceptance notice found. However, because the Alpöge-Bhargava-Ho-Shnidman paper independently proves the identical conclusion for the exact case this bullet asks about (all number fields) and is already published in Inventiones Mathematicae with expert digestion (Quanta) and an independent alternative proof of its key lemma (Poonen), the bullet's question is resolved regardless of the Koymans-Pagano paper's individual publication status. If a stricter reading required every contributing paper to be individually journal-published before calling the bullet 'resolved', this would instead be 'claimed' pending final publication of the Koymans-Pagano preprint.
what_would_settle_it: Direct confirmation of the Koymans-Pagano paper's journal acceptance (or continued preprint status), and any expert survey or Bourbaki-seminar-style digestion explicitly stating both proofs are fully verified and uncontested, would remove any residual ambiguity.
